What started with feeding a few stray cats has turned into saving more than 3,000 lives 🐈💗

Meet Dina Taji, co-founder of @dubaistreetkitties , who has dedicated years of her life to rescuing, caring for and finding homes for Dubai’s most vulnerable cats.

We visited her sanctuary, home to around 650 cats, to hear her story and understand what really goes into giving these animals a second chance.

And if there’s one thing Dina wants more people to know, it’s that adoption is the biggest help they need right now.

Watch our interview, read the full story on pike.digital and, if you’ve been thinking about welcoming a little furry friend into your life, this might be your sign 💌

🐾 @dubaistreetkitties
reels.transcript: Sometimes instead of waiting for someone else to act, we might just be their only chance that will help them survive. My name is Dina Taji, you might know me from Dubai Street Kitty Sanctuary here in the UAE, where we care for about 650 cats and so far I've rescued around 3,000 cats. When we saw the number of cats that were being dumped either by breeders or people going back to their home country, that's when my friend and I realized we need to create a sanctuary for them. Someone sent me a picture of a cat hanging on a highway fence, and it was hanging all the way at the top because it was absolutely freaked out because of the cars. And it was like around 6:00 in the morning. I saw that I jumped out of bed, immediately drove over there, just to find the cat still in the exact same position. It bit my hand so deep, but I was like, I'm not letting go, and I managed to get the cat to the vet. This is our number one thing. If you were to ask me right now, what is the one thing that you would need the most for your sanctuary is getting these cats rehomed. This is the most important thing. People that see this issue and they want to adopt because they want to help, but they they're hesitant because they don't know what to do. Maybe they never had a pet before. That's why it's really great. Instead of committing and actually going for an adoption process, you can do what's called fostering that that really make you realize that love is not just a human need. It's a universal need. And all they want to do is just be loved, feel safe and cared for. Aw, it's okay. They all just want to be loved.
